info.title: Keylight Management API
info.summary: Token-authenticated JSON API for managing a Keylight tenant from the terminal, CI, or an AI agent.
info.description:
The Keylight Management API is the control plane behind the `keylight` CLI: one API, many thin clients. Every endpoint is tenant-scoped by the bearer token — there is no tenant id in the path.

## Authentication

Send a personal access token as `Authorization: Bearer klm_...`. Tokens are minted in the dashboard (Settings -> API tokens), shown once, and carry a fixed set of scopes. A missing or bad token is `401`; a token without the required scope is `403`. This is a plain bearer PAT, not OAuth2 — the scopes below are attached to the token at creation, not negotiated per request.

## Scopes

`products:read`, `products:write`, `licenses:read`, `licenses:write`, `integrations:read`, `integrations:write`, `customers:read`, `customers:write`, `usage:read`, and `danger`. The `danger` scope is required *in addition* to the resource scope for every confirm-gated operation. Each operation lists the exact scopes it needs in `x-required-scopes`.

## Confirmation gate (dangerous operations)

Destructive, hijack-shaped, or secret-revealing operations are not removed — they are confirm-gated in the style of npm's web login. A gated call with no confirmation header does not execute: it returns `202` with a pending confirmation (`id`, `approveUrl`, `expiresInSeconds`). A human opens `approveUrl` in a dashboard session and approves or denies. The agent polls `GET /v1/confirmations/{id}` until the status is `approved`, `denied`, or `expired`, then re-issues the identical request with `X-Keylight-Confirmation: {id}`. The server verifies the request's parameter hash matches the approved one and consumes the confirmation atomically, so a gated operation executes exactly once even under racing retries. A consumed, denied, expired, or mismatched confirmation is `403`.

## Idempotency

`POST /v1/licenses` and `POST /v1/licenses/import` accept an `Idempotency-Key` request header. The first success is stored for 24h keyed on a hash of the header; a replay with the same key returns the stored response body verbatim with `Idempotent-Replay: true` and does not re-execute.

## Pagination

List endpoints are cursor-paginated: `?cursor=` + `?limit=` (max 100, default 25). Responses are `{ "items": [...], "nextCursor": string | null }`. Ordering is stable (createdAt desc with an id tiebreak). Follow `nextCursor` until it is `null`.

## Errors

Every error is `{ "error": "message" }`. `400` malformed input, `401` bad/revoked token, `402` plan-gated, `403` missing scope or failed confirmation, `404` absent OR cross-tenant (indistinguishable — no existence leak), `405` wrong method, `409` state conflict, `422` semantic validation, `429` rate-limited (with `Retry-After`).

## Secrets

Raw license keys are returned only once, in the mint/remint responses. The SDK key, webhook signing secret, and Gumroad ping URL are each revealed exactly once on their gated write/read paths. List and detail responses never contain a raw key or secret — only masked display forms.

## Polling

The poll-shaped endpoints (`/v1/confirmations/{id}`, `/v1/test-purchase/{id}`) and `/v1/usage` are built to be polled and are cheap to call repeatedly. Honour their `Retry-After`.

## Customer branding
`GET/PATCH /v1/branding` reads or updates this workspace customer identity. `POST /v1/branding/logo` uploads an immutable logo and `DELETE` removes the current reference. Business identity stays separate from owner profile and billing details. The support email is used as Reply-To when present; Keylight never substitutes the owner email.

get.description: The machine-readable OpenAPI 3.1 description of the Management API. Public — no authentication.
Introspect the calling token: the tenant it belongs to, its id, and its scopes. Any valid token works — no scope required.
Poll the status of a confirmation returned by a gated `202`. Cheap to poll. Honour `Retry-After`. Terminal states are `approved`, `denied`, and `expired`; agents must handle all three.

post.description: Store the app's Stripe test-mode keys, enabling test-mode checkout.
Re-check the Stripe price IDs mapped to this app's key types. `skipped` is true when there is nothing to verify (no Stripe connection or no mappings).

patch.description: Partial update — omitted fields keep their current value. `keyTypeId` is immutable.

delete.description: Confirm-gated. Requires the `danger` scope in addition to `products:write`. The server refuses (`409`) while live licenses reference the key type, and refuses to delete the app's only key type. See the confirmation gate in the API description.

get.description: Cursor-paginated. Keys are masked (`displayKey` only). Filter with `?product=` and `?status=`.

post.description: Mint a license manually. The raw `licenseKey` is returned exactly once — store it. Accepts an `Idempotency-Key` header; a replay returns the original result with `Idempotent-Replay: true` and does not double-mint.

201.description: License minted. Contains the raw key (once).

post.description: Import a chunk of legacy licenses (one chunk per call). The server re-validates every row. Accepts an `Idempotency-Key` header; a replay returns the original counts and does not re-import.

get.description: Confirm-gated. Requires the `danger` scope in addition to `licenses:read`. Also plan-gated to Enterprise (`402` otherwise) — the plan check runs before a confirmation is parked. On approval returns a CSV file (`text/csv`).

post.description: Activate a device against a license over HTTPS — no SDK. Enforces the seat limit and returns clean JSON (no lease to decode). Idempotent per device_id.

get.description: Full detail: devices, status, remint lineage, and recent activity. The key is masked.

post.description: Confirm-gated. Requires the `danger` scope in addition to `licenses:write`, and is subject to a stricter rate bucket (30/hour). Already-revoked is `409`.

Re-issue a replacement key for a license. The new raw key is returned once. Body is optional; a bare POST reissues without emailing the customer. A license that cannot be reminted in its current state (revoked, or not in good standing) is `409`.

sendEmail.description: Email the linked customer their replacement key.

201.description: License reminted. Contains the new raw key (once).

post.description: Free a seat by deactivating one activated device instance.

instanceId.description: The device instance id from the license's devices list.

get.description: Confirm-gated read of the live SDK key (`sdk_live_...`). Requires the `danger` scope in addition to `integrations:read`. Legacy pre-encryption keys cannot be revealed (`409`) — rotate instead. The key is returned once on the approving response.

post.description: Confirm-gated. Requires the `danger` scope in addition to `integrations:write`. Rotation invalidates the key baked into every shipped app build immediately — the approval screen states this. The new key is returned once.

get.description: Payment providers and their status per app, plus Stripe Connect status.

post.description: Returns the Stripe OAuth authorize URL to open in a browser (Connect onboarding cannot be terminal-only). Body optional; empty means live mode. Nothing is persisted here — state changes on the OAuth callback.

get.description: Poll the Stripe connection status (live and sandbox slots + per-app enablement).

post.description: Connect a payment provider. Env-capable providers (paddle, lemonsqueezy, polar) configure one environment slot per call and require `environment`; omitting it returns 422. `apiKey` is required for Paddle (its credentials are verified against the Paddle API) and optional for Lemon Squeezy and Polar, where a blank value preserves the stored key. Gumroad ignores the request body and returns a generated ping URL exactly once.

422.description: environment is missing for an env-capable provider.

post.description: Confirm-gated. Requires the `danger` scope in addition to `integrations:write`. Only Gumroad supports rotation (others: disconnect and reconnect — `400`). The current ping URL stops working immediately; the new ping URL is returned once.

delete.description: Disconnect a merchant-of-record provider. For Paddle, `?environment=sandbox|live` targets one slot (defaults to live); an invalid value is `422`. A not-connected provider is `404`.

parameters.name: environment
parameters.description: Env-capable providers (paddle, lemonsqueezy, polar): which environment slot to remove. Removing one slot keeps the other connected.

remainingEnvironments.description: Paddle only — true when the other environment slot is still connected.

post.summary: Configure a provider on an app
post.description: Enable/disable a provider for one app, or set its price mappings. Provide exactly one of: `enabled` (toggle), `prices` (keyTypeId -> price id), or `environments` (Paddle per-environment maps). `enabled` cannot be combined with the mapping fields — the mappings set the enabled state themselves.

get.description: The current license-delivery webhook settings. Never returns the signing secret — only whether one is on file.

put.description: Confirm-gated (delivery-hijack risk — license keys get POSTed to this URL). Requires the `danger` scope in addition to `integrations:write`. `url` is always required (send `null` to clear). The signing secret is returned once on the approving response.

200.description: Webhook settings saved. Contains the signing secret (once).

post.description: The email is the identity: re-posting an existing email updates the name instead of erroring. `201` on first create, `200` on an upsert of an existing customer.

get.description: Linked licenses (keys masked), payments, revenue total, and license activity.

post.summary: Link a license to a customer
post.description: Attach an existing license to this customer. The customer must already exist (create it first via POST /v1/customers) — `404` otherwise.

licenseId.description: The license id (hex key hash) from list/detail/mint.

patch.description:
Set, clear, or change the entitlement override on one of this customer's licenses. Entitlements live on the license, so the target license is named in the body; a license not linked to this customer is `404`.

Send either `entitlements` (a full replace; `null` clears the override and the key-type default applies again) or `add` and/or `remove`. `add`/`remove` change only the entitlements named, starting from the ones in effect, and are applied atomically with every other write to the license, so two servers editing different entitlements can't undo each other. A change that leaves the set as it was writes nothing. Read the current entitlements with `GET /v1/licenses/{licenseId}`.

entitlements.description: Full replace, or null to clear the override. Not combined with add/remove.

add.description: Entitlements to add to the ones in effect.

remove.description: Entitlements to remove from the ones in effect.

get.description: Activation and validation stats for the tenant. Cheap to poll. `?days` trims the daily series (default 30, max 60).

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: Number of days in the daily series (1-60).

post.description: Run an end-to-end purchase simulation. Mints a real (test-marked) license through the production issuance pipeline and emails it to the tenant's own inbox. Returns the masked key plus a run id pollable for 24h.

get.description: Poll a test-purchase run by id. Cheap to poll. A foreign or unknown run id is `404`.

post.description: RFC 8628. Returns a device_code (secret, poll with it) and a short user_code the human enters at verification_uri. No auth.

scopes.description: Requested scopes; defaults to all except danger.

post.description: Poll with device_code at the returned interval. 200 with status pending|denied|approved; the token is returned once when approved.
Self-revoke: revokes the bearer token used for this request. Backs keylight logout. Idempotent.

patch.description: Partial update. Omitted fields are preserved; explicit null clears a field. Branding fields require Starter or above. Support email is available on every plan.

422.description: Invalid input or unavailable plan capability.

post.description: Upload PNG, JPEG or WebP up to 2 MB. The server validates image bytes and dimensions and returns an immutable HTTPS asset URL.

bearerToken.description: A Keylight personal access token, minted in the dashboard (Settings -> API tokens). Send as `Authorization: Bearer klm_...`. Each token carries a fixed scope set; per-operation scope requirements are listed in `x-required-scopes`. Confirm-gated operations additionally require the `danger` scope.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous page's `nextCursor`. Omit for the first page.

ConfirmationId.name: id
ConfirmationId.description: The confirmation id (32 hex chars) from a gated `202`.

ConfirmationHeader.name: X-Keylight-Confirmation
ConfirmationHeader.description: The approved confirmation id to consume. Omit on the first call (the server returns a `202` pending confirmation); supply it to re-issue an approved gated call. The request parameters must be byte-identical to the ones that were approved.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: A client-chosen key that makes this call safe to retry. The first success is cached for 24h; a replay with the same key returns the stored body with `Idempotent-Replay: true` and does not re-execute.

KeyTypeId.name: keyTypeId
KeyTypeId.description: The key type id within the app.

LicenseId.name: licenseId
LicenseId.description: The license id — the sha256 key hash (hex) from list/detail/mint.

CustomerId.name: customerId
CustomerId.description: The customer id — the sha256 email hash (64 hex chars).

Provider.name: provider
Provider.description: A merchant-of-record provider slug (e.g. `paddle`, `gumroad`, `lemonsqueezy`, `polar`). Not `stripe` — Stripe has dedicated endpoints.

RunId.name: runId
RunId.description: The test-purchase run id (32 hex chars).

RetryAfter.description: Minimum seconds to wait before retrying/polling.

IdempotentReplay.description: Present and `true` when this response was replayed from the idempotency cache rather than re-executed.

BadRequest.description: Malformed request (bad JSON or invalid parameters).

Unauthorized.description: Missing, malformed, expired, or revoked token.

PaymentRequired.description: The operation requires a higher Keylight plan.

Forbidden.description: The token lacks a required scope, or a confirmation was denied, expired, already consumed, or its parameters did not match.

NotFound.description: The resource does not exist, or belongs to another tenant (indistinguishable — no existence leak).

MethodNotAllowed.description: The HTTP method is not supported on this path.

Conflict.description: The request conflicts with the resource's current state (e.g. already revoked, live licenses reference the key type, the only key type).

Unprocessable.description: The request was well-formed but semantically invalid.

RateLimited.description: Rate limited. Retry after the `Retry-After` header.

PendingConfirmation.description: The operation is confirm-gated and no valid confirmation was supplied. A pending confirmation was created — open `approveUrl` in a dashboard session, then poll `GET /v1/confirmations/{id}` and re-issue with the `X-Keylight-Confirmation` header once approved.

approveUrl.description: Open in a dashboard session to approve or deny.

expiresInSeconds.description: Seconds until the pending confirmation expires.

Product.description: An app. Encrypted Stripe override secrets are stripped from API responses. Additional settings fields may appear.

integrationMode.description: How the app integrates with Keylight: `sdk` (ship a Keylight SDK) or `api` (call the HTTP API directly, no SDK). Always present in responses; defaults to `sdk`.
Integration mode for the app: `sdk` or `api`. Defaults to `sdk`.

UpdateProductBody.description: Partial update — omitted fields are unchanged.

KeyType.description: A license key type on an app.

UpdateKeyTypeBody.description: Partial update — omitted fields are unchanged. `keyTypeId` is immutable.

License.description: A license in list form. The raw key is never present — only `displayKey` (masked).

id.description: The license id (sha256 key hash, hex).

displayKey.description: Masked display form of the key.

sendEmail.description: Deliver the key to the linked customer by email (default off for API mints).

licenseKey.description: The plaintext key — returned once, never retrievable again.
The plaintext replacement key — returned once.

remintedFromId.description: The id of the license this replaced.

license_key.description: Existing key to preserve; empty to mint a fresh one.

entitlements.description: The entitlements the app gets for this license: the per-license override if one is set, otherwise the key type's defaults.

overridden.description: True when a per-license override is set.

created.description: True on a genuine create, false when an existing customer was refreshed.

totalRevenueCents.description: Lifetime revenue in `revenueCurrency` only. Payments in other currencies are listed in `revenueByCurrency` and never added in.

revenueCurrency.description: The customer's main currency (lower-case ISO code, the one with the most revenue), or null with no payments.

revenueByCurrency.description: Lifetime revenue per currency, largest first.

entitlements.description: The effective entitlements after the change.

overridden.description: Whether an override is now in place.

ConnectIntegrationBody.description: Env-capable providers (paddle, lemonsqueezy, polar) submit `environment` plus `webhookSecret`, and `apiKey` where the provider needs one. Gumroad ignores the request body entirely — it generates its own token and returns a ping URL.

environment.description: Env-capable providers (paddle, lemonsqueezy, polar): required — which environment slot to configure.

webhookSecret.description: Env-capable providers: the environment's webhook signing secret.

apiKey.description: Env-capable providers: required for Paddle, optional for Lemon Squeezy and Polar (a blank value preserves the stored key).

environment.description: Env-capable providers — the slot that was configured.

alreadyConnected.description: True when the provider was already connected (no-op).

pingUrl.description: Gumroad only — the generated ping URL, returned once.

ProductIntegrationBody.description: Provide exactly one of `enabled`, `prices`, or `environments`. `enabled` cannot be combined with the mapping fields.

enabled.description: Enable/disable the provider for this app (no mapping changes).

mappedPrices.description: Present on a mapping update — how many prices are now mapped.

EnvironmentStatus.description: Per-environment credential and mapping state for an env-capable provider (paddle, lemonsqueezy, polar).

products.description: App ids with this provider enabled.

environments.description: Env-capable providers only (paddle, lemonsqueezy, polar) — per-environment credential/mapping state.

hasSigningSecret.description: Whether a signing secret is on file — never the secret itself.

url.description: The license-delivery webhook URL (https, public host). null clears it.

signingSecret.description: The signing secret — returned once, only on the approving response.

licenseKeyMasked.description: Masked license key — the raw key is emailed to the tenant's own inbox.

email.description: The inbox the test key was emailed to.
